title: The Conviction of the Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The conviction of the Spirit is the work by which the Holy Spirit exposes sin, righteousness, and judgment so sinners may see their need for Christ and believers may turn from sin in repentance.
summary: The conviction of the Spirit is the work by which the Holy Spirit exposes sin, righteousness, and judgment so sinners may see their need for Christ and believers may turn from sin in repentance.
christFocus: The Spirit convicts in order to lead people to the truth of Christ. He does not merely produce guilt; He exposes sin so sinners may flee to the Savior and believers may walk in holiness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus taught that the Spirit would convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment. The Spirit exposes what people often hide, excuse, deny, or misunderstand.

Conviction is not the same as condemnation for those in Christ. Condemnation crushes without hope, but conviction tells the truth in order to lead to repentance, faith, and restoration.

The Spirit uses the Word of God to pierce the heart. At Pentecost, hearers were cut to the heart and called to repent. True conviction brings sinners face to face with God’s holiness and Christ’s saving mercy.

Believers continue to need conviction. The Spirit faithfully exposes bitterness, pride, unbelief, lust, dishonesty, and every sin that resists Christ’s rule.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often confuse conviction with shame, fear, or self-hatred. The Spirit’s work is holy and truthful, but it is not hopeless. He reveals sin so that people may come into the light and receive grace in Christ.

This doctrine is especially important in recovery and discipleship. Real freedom requires more than feeling better; it requires the Spirit’s truthful exposure and the Savior’s cleansing mercy.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not run from the Spirit’s conviction. When God exposes sin, confess it honestly, turn from it, and come to Christ for mercy and cleansing. Learn to distinguish the Spirit’s truthful conviction from the enemy’s hopeless accusation, and let conviction lead you into repentance and renewed obedience.
